validity.recommendation: Check who will operate the connecting pipeline. Gazprom is named for construction. A trade page names Gazprom Dobycha Noyabrsk, and a December 2025 Interfax report has Gazprom Neft developing the two fields.
validity.researcher_notes: The November 2024 order entrusts Gazprom with building the pipeline. The operator of the finished line is not stated by any loadable page.

fills.researcher_notes: The Interfax report on the August 2024 government order gives 10.72 billion cubic meters a year for the connecting pipeline.

The November 2024 government order, as reported by Neftegaz, entrusts Gazprom with building the connecting pipeline. A construction trade page says the project will be run by Gazprom Dobycha Noyabrsk. No loadable page names the operator of the finished line, so the value stays and a person should check it.

The November 2024 government order, read through Neftegaz, entrusts Gazprom with the construction of this connecting pipeline. It assigns the work and does not state ownership shares, so tier is medium.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: A construction trade page reports that work has started on connecting the Tas-Yuryakh and Verkhnevilyuchan fields to Power of Siberia. The page shows a day and month but no year. The Interfax report on the August 2024 order and the November 2024 order both treat the pipeline as still to be built.

cross_row_leads.finding: A December 2025 report has Gazprom Neft developing the Tas-Yuryakh and Verkhnevilyuchan fields, which bears on who operates the connecting pipeline.
